NKJV.1: Where has your beloved gone,  O fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned aside, That we may seek him with you?
NKJV.2: My beloved has gone to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed his flock in the gardens, And to gather lilies.
NKJV.3: I am my beloved’s, And my beloved is mine. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
NKJV.4: O my love, you are as beautiful as Tirzah, Lovely as Jerusalem, Awesome as an army with banners!
NKJV.5: Turn your eyes away from me, For they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats Going down from Gilead.
NKJV.6: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep Which have come up from the washing; Every one bears twins, And none is barren among them.
NKJV.7: Like a piece of pomegranate Are your temples behind your veil.
NKJV.8: There are sixty queens And eighty concubines, And virgins without number.
NKJV.9: My dove, my perfect one, Is the only one, The only one of her mother, The favorite of the one who bore her. The daughters saw her And called her blessed, The queens and the concubines, And they praised her.
NKJV.10: Who is she who looks forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Awesome as an army with banners?
NKJV.11: I went down to the garden of nuts To see the verdure of the valley, To see whether the vine had budded And the pomegranates had bloomed.
NKJV.12: Before I was even aware, My soul had made me As the chariots of my noble people.
NKJV.13: Return, return, O Shulamite; Return, return, that we may look upon you! What would you see in the Shulamite— As it were, the dance of the two camps?

NLT.1:
Where has your lover gone,
O woman of rare beauty?
Which way did he turn
so we can help you find him?
NLT.2:
My lover has gone down to his garden,
to his spice beds,
to browse in the gardens
and gather the lilies.
NLT.3:
I am my lover’s, and my lover is mine.
He browses among the lilies.
NLT.4:
You are beautiful, my darling,
like the lovely city of Tirzah.
Yes, as beautiful as Jerusalem,
as majestic as an army with billowing banners.
NLT.5:
Turn your eyes away,
for they overpower me.
Your hair falls in waves,
like a flock of goats winding down the slopes of Gilead.
NLT.6:
Your teeth are as white as sheep
that are freshly washed.
Your smile is flawless,
each tooth matched with its twin.
NLT.7:
Your cheeks are like rosy pomegranates
behind your veil.
NLT.8:
Even among sixty queens
and eighty concubines
and countless young women,
NLT.9:
I would still choose my dove, my perfect one —
the favorite of her mother,
dearly loved by the one who bore her.
The young women see her and praise her;
even queens and royal concubines sing her praises:
NLT.10:
“Who is this, arising like the dawn,
as fair as the moon,
as bright as the sun,
as majestic as an army with billowing banners?”
NLT.11:
I went down to the grove of walnut trees
and out to the valley to see the new spring growth,
to see whether the grapevines had budded
or the pomegranates were in bloom.
NLT.12:
Before I realized it,
my strong desires had taken me to the chariot of a noble man.
NLT.13:
Return, return to us, O maid of Shulam.
Come back, come back, that we may see you again. Young Man
Why do you stare at this young woman of Shulam,
as she moves so gracefully between two lines of dancers?

MSG.1:
So where has this love of yours gone,
fair one?
Where on earth can he be?
Can we help you look for him?
MSG.2:
Never mind. My lover is already on his way to his garden,
to browse among the flowers, touching the colors and forms.
MSG.3:
I am my lover's and my lover is mine.
He caresses the sweet-smelling flowers.
MSG.4:
Dear, dear friend and lover,
you're as beautiful as Tirzah, city of delights,
Lovely as Jerusalem, city of dreams,
the ravishing visions of my ecstasy.
MSG.5:
Your beauty is too much for me—I'm in over my head.
I'm not used to this! I can't take it in.
Your hair flows and shimmers
like a flock of goats in the distance
streaming down a hillside in the sunshine.
MSG.6:
Your smile is generous and full—
expressive and strong and clean.
MSG.7:
Your veiled cheeks
are soft and radiant.
MSG.8:
There's no one like her on earth,
never has been, never will be.
MSG.9:
She's a woman beyond compare.
My dove is perfection,
Pure and innocent as the day she was born,
and cradled in joy by her mother.
Everyone who came by to see her
exclaimed and admired her—
All the fathers and mothers, the neighbors and friends,
blessed and praised her:
MSG.10:
"Has anyone ever seen anything like this—
dawn-fresh, moon-lovely, sun-radiant,
ravishing as the night sky with its galaxies of stars?"
MSG.11:
One day I went strolling through the orchard,
looking for signs of spring,
Looking for buds about to burst into flower,
anticipating readiness, ripeness.
MSG.12:
Before I knew it my heart was raptured,
carried away by lofty thoughts!
MSG.13:
Dance, dance, dear Shulammite, Angel-Princess!
Dance, and we'll feast our eyes on your grace!
Everyone wants to see the Shulammite dance
her victory dances of love and peace.

NET.1: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Where has your beloved turned? Tell us, that we may seek him with you.
NET.2: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the flowerbeds of balsam spices, to graze in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
NET.3: I am my lover’s and my lover is mine; he grazes among the lilies.
NET.4: My darling, you are as beautiful as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as awe-inspiring as bannered armies!
NET.5: Turn your eyes away from me — they overwhelm me! Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilead.
NET.6: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin; not one of them is missing.
NET.7: Like a slice of pomegranate is your forehead behind your veil.
NET.8: There may be sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and young women without number.

NET.10: “Who is this who appears like the dawn? Beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, awe-inspiring as the stars in procession?”
NET.11: I went down to the orchard of walnut trees, to look for the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines had budded or if the pomegranates were in bloom.
NET.12: I was beside myself with joy! There please give me your myrrh, O daughter of my princely people.
NET.13: (7:1) Turn , turn, O Perfect One! Turn, turn, that I may stare at you! Why do you gaze upon the Perfect One like the dance of the Mahanaim?
